metadata.title: Fully Homomorphic Encryption over the Integers
metadata.authors: Marten van Dijk, Craig Gentry, Shai Halevi, Vinod Vaikuntanathan
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: 2-universal hash family
nodes.statement: A family $H$ of hash functions from $X$ to $Y$ (finite sets) is $2$-universal if for all distinct $x, x' \in X$, $\Pr_{h \leftarrow H}[h(x) = h(x')] = 1/|Y|$.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-uniform distribution
nodes.statement: A distribution $D$ over a finite domain $X$ is $\epsilon$-uniform if its statistical distance from uniform is at most $\epsilon$, where statistical distance is $\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x \in X}|D_1(x) - D_2(x)|$.

nodes.name: Simplified Leftover Hash Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $H$ be a $2$-universal family of hash functions from $X$ to $Y$. If $h \leftarrow H$ and $x \leftarrow X$ are uniform and independent, then $(h, h(x))$ is $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{|Y|/|X|}$-uniform over $H \times Y$.
assumptions: $h \leftarrow H$ and $x \leftarrow X$ chosen uniformly and independently
conclusions: $(h, h(x))$ is $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{|Y|/|X|}$-uniform over $H \times Y$

nodes.name: Correct Homomorphic Decryption
nodes.statement: Scheme $E = (\text{KeyGen}, \text{Encrypt}, \text{Decrypt}, \text{Evaluate})$ is correct for circuit $C$ if for any keys, plaintexts $m_i$, and ciphertexts $c_i \leftarrow \text{Encrypt}(pk, m_i)$: $\text{Decrypt}(sk, \text{Evaluate}(pk, C, \vec{c})) = C(m_1,\ldots,m_t)$.

nodes.name: Homomorphic Encryption / Fully Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: $E$ is homomorphic for a class $\mathcal{C}$ of circuits if it is correct for all $C \in \mathcal{C}$. $E$ is fully homomorphic if it is correct for all boolean circuits.

nodes.name: Compact Homomorphic Encryption
nodes.statement: $E$ is compact if there exists a fixed polynomial bound $b(\lambda)$ such that for any keys, circuit $C$, and ciphertexts $\vec{c}$, the size of $\text{Evaluate}(pk, C, \vec{c})$ is at most $b(\lambda)$ bits, independently of $|C|$.

nodes.name: Augmented Decryption Circuits
nodes.statement: For security parameter $\lambda$, $D_E(\lambda)$ is the set of two circuits taking secret key and two ciphertexts: one decrypts both and adds the resulting plaintext bits mod $2$, the other decrypts both and multiplies them mod $2$.

nodes.name: Bootstrappable Encryption
nodes.statement: Homomorphic scheme $E$ with correctness class $C_E(\lambda)$ is bootstrappable if $D_E(\lambda) \subseteq C_E(\lambda)$ for every $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Gentry's Bootstrapping Theorem
nodes.statement: There is an efficient transformation that, given a bootstrappable scheme $E$ and parameter $d=d(\lambda)$, outputs a scheme $E^{(d)}$ that is compact and homomorphic for all circuits of depth up to $d$, with semantic security loss $\varepsilon/\ell^d$.
conclusions: $E^{(d)}$ is compact (Decrypt circuit identical to $E$)
$E^{(d)}$ is homomorphic for circuits of depth up to $d$
Any attack with advantage $\varepsilon$ against $E^{(d)}$ converts to attack on $E$ with advantage $\geq \varepsilon/\ell^d$

nodes.name: Distribution $D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$
nodes.statement: For odd $\eta$-bit positive integer $p$: $D_{\gamma,\rho}(p) = \{q \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathbb{Z} \cap [0, 2^\gamma/p),\ r \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathbb{Z} \cap (-2^\rho, 2^\rho) : x = pq + r\}$.

nodes.name: Parameter Constraints (Somewhat Homomorphic Scheme)
nodes.statement: Parameters satisfy: $\rho = \omega(\log \lambda)$ (anti brute-force noise); $\eta \geq \rho \cdot \Theta(\lambda \log^2 \lambda)$ (deep enough circuits); $\gamma = \omega(\eta^2 \log \lambda)$ (anti-lattice attacks); $\tau \geq \gamma + \omega(\log \lambda)$ (leftover hash lemma); $\rho' = \rho + \omega(\log \lambda)$.

nodes.name: Somewhat Homomorphic Scheme (DGHV) -- KeyGen / Encrypt / Decrypt / Evaluate
nodes.statement: Public-key encryption over the integers: secret key is an odd $\eta$-bit $p$; public key is $\tau+1$ samples $x_i \leftarrow D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$; encryption sets $c \gets m + 2r + 2\sum_{i \in S} x_i \pmod{x_0}$; decryption returns $(c \bmod p) \bmod 2$.

nodes.name: KeyGen
nodes.statement: Sample $p \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} (2\mathbb{Z}+1) \cap [2^{\eta-1}, 2^\eta)$. Sample $x_i \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$ for $i = 0, \ldots, \tau$, relabel so $x_0$ is largest, restart unless $x_0$ is odd and $r_p(x_0)$ is even. Output $pk = \langle x_0, \ldots, x_\tau \rangle$.

nodes.name: Encrypt
nodes.statement: On bit $m \in \{0,1\}$: choose random subset $S \subseteq \{1,\ldots,\tau\}$ and random $r \in (-2^{\rho'}, 2^{\rho'})$; output $c \gets [m + 2r + 2\sum_{i \in S} x_i]_{x_0}$.

nodes.name: Evaluate
nodes.statement: Given binary circuit $C_E$ with $t$ inputs and ciphertexts $c_1,\ldots,c_t$: apply integer addition and multiplication gates of $C_E$ over the integers and return resulting integer.

nodes.name: Decrypt
nodes.statement: Output $m' \gets (c \bmod p) \bmod 2$. Equivalently (since $p$ is odd) $m' \gets [c - \lfloor c/p \rceil]_2 = (c \bmod 2) \oplus (\lfloor c/p \rceil \bmod 2)$.

nodes.name: Permitted Circuit / Permitted Polynomial
nodes.statement: $C_E$ is the set of mod-$2$ arithmetic circuits such that for any $\alpha \geq 1$ and integer inputs of magnitude $< 2^{\alpha(\rho'+2)}$, the generalized integer circuit's output has magnitude $\leq 2^{\alpha(\eta-4)}$. $P_E$ is the set of polynomials $f$ satisfying $d \leq (\eta - 4 - \log|\vec{f}|)/(\rho'+2)$.

nodes.name: Permitted polynomial degree bound
nodes.statement: $d \leq \dfrac{\eta - 4 - \log |\vec{f}|}{\rho' + 2}$ \quad (Eq. 1)

nodes.name: Correctness of the Somewhat Homomorphic Scheme
nodes.statement: The somewhat homomorphic scheme of Section 3.1 is correct for $C_E$ (the set of permitted circuits).
assumptions: Parameters satisfy the constraints of Section 3
conclusions: $\text{Decrypt}(sk, \text{Evaluate}(pk, C, \vec{c})) = C(m_1,\ldots,m_t)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3 (Appendix A)
nodes.statement: Show fresh ciphertexts have form $c = ap + (2b+m)$ with $|2b+m| \leq \tau 2^{\rho+3}$ (Lemma A.1), then show ciphertexts output by Evaluate also have this form with $|2b+m| < p/8$ (Lemma A.2). Together they imply $[c]_p = 2b+m$ so $m = [[c]_p]_2$.

nodes.name: Permitted-polynomial sufficient condition
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be a boolean circuit with $t$ inputs, $C^\dagger$ its integer counterpart, $f$ the multivariate polynomial it computes of degree $d$. If $|\vec{f}| \cdot (2^{\rho'+2})^d \leq 2^{\eta-4}$ then $C \in C_E$.
assumptions: $C$ boolean circuit, $C^\dagger$ integer circuit, $f$ multivariate polynomial of degree $d$
conclusions: $C \in C_E$ (i.e., the scheme can homomorphically evaluate $f$)

nodes.name: Approximate GCD Problem
nodes.statement: The $(\rho, \eta, \gamma)$-approximate-gcd problem: given polynomially many samples from $D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$ for a randomly chosen $\eta$-bit odd integer $p$, output $p$.

nodes.name: $(\rho, \eta, \gamma)$-Approximate GCD Problem
nodes.statement: Given polynomially many integers $x_i = q_i p + r_i$ near multiples of a hidden $\eta$-bit odd integer $p$ (with $|r_i| < 2^\rho$, $q_i \in [0, 2^\gamma/p)$), recover $p$.

nodes.name: Security Reduction: Encryption to Approximate-GCD
nodes.statement: Fix scheme parameters $(\rho, \rho', \eta, \gamma, \tau)$. Any attack $A$ with advantage $\varepsilon$ on the encryption scheme can be converted into an algorithm $B$ for $(\rho, \eta, \gamma)$-approximate-gcd with success probability $\geq \varepsilon/2$ in time poly in $A$'s runtime, $\lambda$, and $1/\varepsilon$.
conclusions: Algorithm $B$ solves $(\rho, \eta, \gamma)$-approximate-gcd with probability $\geq \varepsilon/2$
Running time of $B$ is polynomial in $A$'s runtime, $\lambda$, $1/\varepsilon$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.2 (Reduction to Approximate-GCD)
nodes.statement: Build solver $B$ in four steps: (1) construct public key from approximate-gcd samples, (2) Learn-LSB subroutine using $A$ as LSB oracle for $q_p(z)$, (3) binary-GCD using the LSB oracle, (4) recover $p$ from output. Success probability bounded via Lemma 4.3.

nodes.name: Step 1 -- Creating a public key
nodes.statement: $B$ draws $\tau + 1$ samples $x_0, \ldots, x_\tau \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$, relabels so $x_0$ is largest, restarts unless $x_0$ is odd, outputs $pk = \langle x_0, \ldots, x_\tau \rangle$. If $r_p(x_0)$ is even, the distribution matches the scheme.

nodes.name: Step 2 -- Subroutine Learn-LSB for high-accuracy LSB predictor
nodes.statement: Subroutine: for $j = 1$ to $\text{poly}(\lambda)/\varepsilon$, choose noise $r_j \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow}(-2^{\rho'}, 2^{\rho'})$, $m_j \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow}\{0,1\}$, subset $S_j \subseteq_R \{1,\ldots,\tau\}$; set $c_j \gets [z + m_j + 2r_j + 2\sum_{k \in S_j} x_k]_{x_0}$; call $a_j \gets A(pk, c_j)$; set $b_j \gets a_j \oplus \text{parity}(z) \oplus m_j$. Output majority vote among the $b_j$'s.

nodes.name: Step 3 -- Binary GCD using LSB oracle
nodes.statement: Use binary-GCD algorithm of Knuth on two integers $z_1, z_2 = q_p(z_i) p + r_p(z_i)$: swap if $z_2 > z_1$; learn parity of $q_p(z_i)$ via LSB oracle; if both odd replace $z_1 \gets z_1 - z_2$ and $b_1 \gets 0$; for each $z_i$ with $b_i = 0$ replace by $(z_i - \text{parity}(z_i))/2$. Noise stays bounded so this corresponds to binary GCD on $q_p(z_i)$'s; after $O(\gamma)$ iterations $z_2' = 0$ and $q_p(z_1')$ is odd part of $\gcd(q_p(z_1), q_p(z_2))$.

nodes.name: Step 4 -- Recovering $p$
nodes.statement: $B$ draws $z_1^*, z_2^* \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} D_{\gamma,\rho}(p)$ and runs binary-GCD; with probability $\geq \pi^2/6 \approx 0.6$ the odd part of $\gcd(q_p(z_1^*), q_p(z_2^*)) = 1$ giving output $\tilde{z} = p + r$ with $|r| \leq 2^\rho$. Repeat binary-GCD on $z_1^*, \tilde{z}$; the parity bits encountered spell binary representation of $q_p(z_1^*)$. Recover $p = \lfloor z_1^*/q_p(z_1^*) \rceil$.

nodes.name: Step 5 -- Success probability analysis
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be the set of $p \in [2^{\eta-1}, 2^\eta)$ for which $A$'s advantage is $\geq \varepsilon/2$. By counting, $|P|/|\text{odd in interval}| \geq \varepsilon/2$. For each $p \in P$, KeyGen outputs $pk \in PK_p$ (with advantage $\geq \varepsilon/4$) with probability $\geq \varepsilon/4$. Conditioning on the good event $G$ (probability $1/2$) and applying Lemma 4.3, $B$ recovers $p$ with probability $\geq (1/2)(\varepsilon/4 - \text{negl})$. Repeating $(8/\varepsilon)\omega(\log\lambda)$ times yields overwhelming success, giving overall success $\geq \varepsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Reduction Ciphertext Distribution Lemma
nodes.statement: Fix parameters and any $sk = p$. For random $pk = \langle x_0, \ldots, x_\tau \rangle$ from KeyGen and any $x^* \in [0, 2^\gamma]$ within $2^\rho$ of a multiple of $p$, the distribution $C_{pk}(x^*) = \{[x^* + 2r + \sum_{i \in S} x_i]_{x_0}\}$ is statistically close to $\text{Encrypt}(pk, [x^*]_2)$ with overwhelming probability over $(sk, pk)$.
conclusions: With overwhelming probability over $(sk, pk)$, $C_{pk}(x^*)$ is statistically negligibly close to $\text{Encrypt}(pk, m = [x^*]_2)$

nodes.name: Subset-sum Leftover Hash Lemma
nodes.statement: Set $x_1, \ldots, x_T \leftarrow_R \mathbb{Z}_M$ uniformly and independently, $s \leftarrow_R \{0,1\}^T$, and $x_{T+1} \gets \sum_{i=1}^{T} s_i x_i \bmod M$. Then $(x_1,\ldots,x_{T+1})$ is $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{M/2^T}$-uniform over $\mathbb{Z}_M^{T+1}$.
conclusions: $(x_1,\ldots,x_T, x_{T+1})$ with $x_{T+1} = \sum_i s_i x_i \bmod M$ is $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{M/2^T}$-uniform over $\mathbb{Z}_M^{T+1}$

nodes.name: Squashing Parameters
nodes.statement: Additional parameters $\kappa = \gamma\eta/\rho'$, $\theta = \lambda$, $\Theta = \omega(\kappa \log \lambda)$. There is a sparse subset $S \subset \{1, \ldots, \Theta\}$ of size $\theta$ with $\sum_{i \in S} y_i \approx 1/p \pmod{2}$.

nodes.name: Squashed Decryption Scheme
nodes.statement: Modified bootstrappable variant: augment public key with $\vec{y} = \{y_1, \ldots, y_\Theta\}$ rationals such that a sparse subset of size $\theta$ sums to $\approx 1/p \pmod 2$; secret key becomes the indicator vector $\vec{s}$. Decryption replaces $\lfloor c/p \rceil$ by $\lfloor \sum_i s_i z_i \rceil$ with $z_i = [c^* y_i]_2$.

nodes.name: Squashed KeyGen
nodes.statement: Generate $sk^* = p, pk^*$. Set $x_p \gets \lfloor 2^\kappa/p \rceil$; choose random $\Theta$-bit $\vec{s}$ of Hamming weight $\theta$; set $S = \{i : s_i = 1\}$. Choose $u_i \in \mathbb{Z} \cap [0, 2^{\kappa+1})$ subject to $\sum_{i \in S} u_i = x_p \pmod{2^{\kappa+1}}$. Set $y_i = u_i/2^\kappa$. Output $sk = \vec{s}$, $pk = (pk^*, \vec{y})$.

nodes.name: Squashed Encrypt / Evaluate
nodes.statement: Generate $c^*$ via underlying scheme. For $i \in \{1,\ldots,\Theta\}$ set $z_i \gets [c^* \cdot y_i]_2$ keeping $n = \lceil \log \theta \rceil + 3$ bits of precision after binary point. Output $(c^*, \vec{z})$.

nodes.name: Squashed Decrypt
nodes.statement: Output $m' \gets [c^* - \lfloor \sum_i s_i z_i \rceil]_2$.

nodes.name: Correctness of Squashed Scheme
nodes.statement: The modified (squashed) scheme is correct for $C(P_E)$. Moreover, for every ciphertext $(c^*, \vec{z})$ generated by evaluating a permitted polynomial, $\sum_i s_i z_i$ is within $1/4$ of an integer.
assumptions: Ciphertext $(c^*, \vec{z})$ produced by evaluating a permitted polynomial
conclusions: Modified scheme is correct for $C(P_E)$
$\sum_i s_i z_i$ is within $1/4$ of an integer

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.1 (Squashed Correctness)
nodes.statement: Show $\big[(c^*/p) - \sum_i s_i z_i\big]_2 = [c^* \Delta_p + \sum_i s_i \Delta_i]_2$, then bound $|\sum_i s_i \Delta_i| \leq 1/16$ and $|c^* \Delta_p| < 1/16$ using $|c^*| < 2^{\kappa - 4}$ for outputs of permitted polynomials.

nodes.name: Bootstrappability of the Squashed Scheme
nodes.statement: Let $E$ be the squashed scheme above and $D_E$ the augmented decryption circuits. Then $D_E \subset C(P_E)$. Hence $E$ is bootstrappable, and (by Theorem 2.7) yields homomorphic encryption for circuits of any depth.
assumptions: $E$ is the squashed somewhat-homomorphic scheme of Section 6.1
Parameters set as in Section 3, with $\eta = \rho \cdot \Theta(\lambda \log^2 \lambda)$
conclusions: $D_E \subset C(P_E)$, i.e., $E$ is bootstrappable
Combined with Theorem 2.7, yields a fully homomorphic scheme

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.2 (Bootstrappability)
nodes.statement: Express decryption $m' \gets c^* - \lfloor \sum_i s_i z_i \rceil \bmod 2$ as a permitted polynomial and a polynomial-size circuit using a 3-step decomposition (multiply $s_i z_i$, reduce $\Theta$ rationals to $n+1$ via Hamming-weight Lemma 6.3, sum via three-for-two trick).

nodes.name: Step 1 -- Multiplication: $a_i \gets s_i z_i$
nodes.statement: For $i \in \{1,\ldots,\Theta\}$ set $a_i \gets s_i \cdot z_i$ (so $a_i = z_i$ if $s_i = 1$, else $0$). Performed by a $1$-level sub-circuit of multiplication gates; degree $2$.

nodes.name: Step 2 -- Reduce $\Theta$ rationals to $n+1$ via Hamming-weight columns
nodes.statement: From $\{a_i\}$ generate $\{w_j\}_{j=0}^{n}$ rationals such that $\sum_j w_j = \sum_i a_i \pmod 2$. Use Lemma 6.3: $W_{-j}$ (Hamming weight of column $j$ of bit reps) bounded by $\theta$, expressed by polynomial of degree $\leq \theta$ in the $a_{i,-j}$ (since at most $\theta$ of $a_i$'s nonzero). Total degree at most $\theta$.

nodes.name: Step 3 -- Sum $n+1$ rationals via three-for-two trick
nodes.statement: Sum $w_j$'s using three-for-two trick (reducing 3 numbers to 2 of same sum, $\lceil \log_{3/2} k \rceil + 2$ times) followed by final 2-number sum (using $1/4$ rounding promise this is degree $4$, $9$ terms). With $k = n + 1$, total degree $\leq 32 (n+1)^{1/\log(3/2)} < 32 \log^2 \theta$. Combined with steps 1-2: total degree $\leq 64 \theta \log^2 \theta = 64 \lambda \log^2 \lambda$, augmented circuit $\leq 128 \lambda \log^2 \lambda$.

nodes.name: Hamming-Weight Bit-Polynomial Lemma
nodes.statement: Let $\vec{\sigma} = \langle \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_t \rangle$ be a binary vector with Hamming weight $W$ and binary representation $W_n \ldots W_1 W_0$. Then for every $i \leq n$, the bit $W_i(\vec{\sigma})$ can be expressed as a binary polynomial of degree exactly $2^i$ in $\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_t$. Moreover, all polynomials for $W_0, \ldots, W_i$ are simultaneously computable by an arithmetic circuit of size $2^i \cdot t$.
assumptions: $W = \sum_i 2^i W_i$ binary representation of Hamming weight
conclusions: $W_i(\vec{\sigma}) = e_{2^i}(\vec{\sigma}) \bmod 2$, polynomial of degree exactly $2^i$
All $W_0,\ldots,W_i$ simultaneously computable by circuit of size $2^i \cdot t$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement: Use that $W_i(\vec{\sigma}) = e_{2^i}(\vec{\sigma}) \bmod 2$, where $e_k$ is the $k$-th elementary symmetric polynomial. Compute as coefficients of $P_{\vec{\sigma}}(z) = \prod_{i=1}^{t}(z - \sigma_i)$; only need top coefficients via dynamic programming (size $2^i \cdot t$).

nodes.name: Permitted but not shallow
nodes.statement: The first circuit implementation of the Hamming-weight subroutine is not shallow, but it computes only low-degree polynomials (up to degree $2^i$), so by Lemma 3.5 it is a permitted circuit.

nodes.name: Sparse Subset Sum Hardness Assumption
nodes.statement: Putting hint $\vec{y}$ in the public key induces a Sparse Subset Sum Problem (SSSP) assumption (related to low-weight knapsack). Choose $\theta$ large to avoid brute-force/time-space attacks and $\Theta > \omega(\log \lambda) \cdot \kappa$ to thwart known attacks.

nodes.name: Ciphertext Compression (DGHV)
nodes.statement: Compress final ciphertexts to RSA-modulus size: supplement public key with cyclic group $G = \langle g \rangle$ whose order is divisible by $p$; output $c^* \gets g^c$; decrypt by computing $\text{DL}_g(c^*) \bmod p$ then $\bmod 2$. Requires $p$ smooth and an RSA modulus $N$ with $p | \phi(N)$.
input: Public key augmented with group description $(G, g, N)$
output: Compressed ciphertext $c^* \gets g^c \bmod N$, of size $\log N$

nodes.name: Decision Subgroup Problem
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_0, \pi_1 \in [2^{\eta-1}, 2^\eta - 1]$ distinct integers, $G$ the set of cyclic groups, $\text{GroupGen}^\dagger(\mathcal{G}, \pi, \ell)$ samples a group from $\mathcal{G}$ with generator $g$ of order in $[2^\ell, 2^{\ell+1} - 1]$ divisible by $\pi$. Adversary $A$ has advantage $\varepsilon$ if $|\Pr[A \text{ guesses } b] - 1/2| \geq \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Decision Subgroup Assumption
nodes.statement: For appropriate $\eta, \ell$ and $\text{GroupGen}^\dagger$, the decision subgroup problem is hard for any $\pi_0, \pi_1$.
nodes.origin_citation: Gentry & Ramzan [8] / Cachin, Micali, Stadler [3] (phi-hiding variant)

nodes.name: Security of Compressed Scheme
nodes.statement: If algorithm $A$ breaks semantic security of compressed scheme $E^*$ with advantage $\varepsilon$, then there exist $B_0, B_1$ each running in similar time, where either $B_0$ has advantage $\varepsilon/3$ against the decision subgroup problem or $B_1$ has advantage $\varepsilon/3$ against semantic security of $E$.
assumptions: Algorithm $A$ breaks semantic security of $E^*$ with advantage $\varepsilon$
$E$ is statistically circuit-private somewhat homomorphic scheme
conclusions: $\exists B_0$: advantage $\varepsilon/3$ against decision subgroup problem, OR
$\exists B_1$: advantage $\varepsilon/3$ against semantic security of $E$

nodes.name: Lemma A.1 (Fresh Ciphertext Structure)
nodes.statement: Let $(sk, pk) \leftarrow \text{KeyGen}(\lambda)$, $c \leftarrow \text{Encrypt}(pk, m)$ for $m \in \{0,1\}$. Then $c = a \cdot p + (2b + m)$ for integers $a, b$ with $|2b + m| \leq \tau \cdot 2^{\rho+3}$.
conclusions: $c = a \cdot p + (2b + m)$ for some integers $a, b$
$|2b + m| \leq \tau \cdot 2^{\rho+3}$

nodes.name: Lemma A.2 (Evaluated Ciphertext Structure)
nodes.statement: Let $C \in C_E$ with $t$ inputs. For $c_i \leftarrow \text{Encrypt}(pk, m_i)$, let $m \leftarrow C(m_1, \ldots, m_t)$ and $c \leftarrow \text{Evaluate}(pk, C, c_1, \ldots, c_t)$. Then $c = a \cdot p + (2b + m)$ for integers $a, b$ with $|2b + m| < p/8$.
conclusions: $c = a \cdot p + (2b + m)$, with $|2b + m| < p/8$

nodes.name: Howgrave-Graham Lattice Attack on Two-Element Approximate-GCD
nodes.statement: Howgrave-Graham's lattice attack on the two-element approximate-gcd problem (related to Coppersmith's algorithm) recovers $p$ when $\rho/\gamma < (\eta/\gamma)^2$. The attack does not degrade gracefully outside this regime; for incompatible parameters the relevant lattice may contain exponentially many spurious vectors.

nodes.name: SDA Lattice Attack Defense
nodes.statement: Treating $y_i = x_i/x_0$ as Simultaneous Diophantine Approximation (SDA), Lagarias' LLL-based algorithm tries to find target $\vec{v} = \langle q_0, q_1, \ldots, q_t \rangle \cdot M$. For $t \geq \gamma/\eta$ a $2^{\eta - \rho}$ approximation is needed; this requires time roughly $2^{\gamma/\eta^2}$. Setting $\gamma/\eta^2 = \omega(\log \lambda)$ foils the attack.

nodes.name: Improving FHE Efficiency
nodes.statement: Improve the efficiency of the fully homomorphic scheme (currently complexity $\tilde{O}(\lambda^{10})$ for somewhat-homomorphic part) to the extent possible while preserving the hardness of the approximate-gcd problem.
